query: Consider the following context: Constituent phases and their corresponding phase transformations are important in developing alloys. In that context, which method can be used for control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The use of density functional theory (DFT) calculations can effectively control phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni High-Entropy Alloys (HEAs) by predicting the thermodynamic stability of various constituent phases and guiding the optimization of alloy composition and processing conditions.

generation.baseline: traditional trial-and-error methods for alloy development
generation.uncertainty: the accuracy of DFT calculations in predicting phase stability and the complexity of HEA systems may introduce uncertainties in the predicted outcome
